08.0.new:
- A BREAK THAT SAYS A SIDE GRANTED SOMETHING NAMES THE GRANT (ASK 586 J3; Panel Build, Build Independent Verdict, and the Shared Library, both copies; the lists are the sides' own sentences from the rounds, rulings 382 and 383):
  - Judges' text, once in each judge's request, after "A shown chain is footing only through its rows and what the other side has granted (pkgBCL).": "THE GRANTS LISTS below give each side's own grant sentences, numbered G<n> with their round. If a break line says a side granted, conceded, dropped or withdrew something, name the grant by its number (G<n>). If the words are not in that side's list, write NOT A LISTED GRANT and quote the words with their round; they are then your reading."
  - The block, served once in each judge's request, directly above the COLLISION POINTS instructions: "[THE GRANTS LISTS -- each side's own grant sentences, gathered from its rounds by code, not by a judge. A sentence stands here because of its words; whether it bears on a link is the judge's to decide." then `DEFENDER: G1 [<round>] "<the sentence>" | ...` and `CHALLENGER: G<k> [<round>] "<the sentence>" | ...]`, or "none" for a side with no grant sentence. One numbering runs through both lists, the defender's first. The sentences are gathered by a copy of the grants finder (the harvester of THE GRANTS LIST) from the rounds as the judge is shown them; no sentence is cut; a bare grant ("I grant it.") is served with the line before it inside the same quotation; markdown marks are dropped and curly quotation marks made straight. When the gathering fails the block reads "[THE GRANTS LISTS -- not available this run.]" and the check below does nothing.
  - The check (rule E-GRT; Send Back Build, Alt Send Back Build, R2 Alt Send Back Build; on the alternate pass only the seated alternate is read): it reads the lists and the rounds from the judge's own request, and only the judge's break lines (a line holding DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN, or a FORCED line). A grant word is grant, grants, granted, granting, concede, concedes, conceded, conceding, dropped or withdrew, outside quotations and not negated (not, never, no, nor, neither, without, n't). The side that granted is the last side named before the word in its "--" clause (a possessive such as "the challenger's reading" does not name it; "the defender's answer" does); else "by the <side>" after the word; else the side whose link the line grades BROKEN; else the side of a FORCED line's ANSWER round; with no side there is no item. A G number is read outside quotations and outside [L2] entries; a number of four digits or more is a Strong's number and is not read. Fault 1: "the line names no G number of the <side>'s list and does not say NOT A LISTED GRANT". Fault 2: "G<n> is not in the <side>'s list". Fault 3: "the words quoted after NOT A LISTED GRANT do not stand in the <side>'s rounds" (or no words are quoted).
  - The item: the judge's whole line is read and stored (flagged_line and response_line). It goes back once: "ENFORCER DISAGREE: GRANT NOT NAMED (ASK 586 J3): your line on <pair> says the <side> "<the grant word>" something, and <fault>. Name the grant by its number from THE GRANTS LISTS (G<n>), or write NOT A LISTED GRANT and quote the <side>'s words with their round; they are then your reading. CHANGE the line, or KEEP it with one of the two. The judge keeps the decision (ruling 428). This item is recorded and counts against no seat."
  - The record: the row's cure_reason carries "GRANT NOT NAMED (E-GRT, ASK 586 J3, fault <n>): record-only, counts against no seat; the judge keeps the decision (ruling 428)". With an answer the row is CURED and response_line holds the judge's whole reply line; with none it carries "NO ANSWER: recorded; not counted". An E-GRT item is never counted as silence and enters no count.
  - Limits: the send-back builders return before this check on a pass where no enforcer reported a violation, as for E-L2G. An E-GRT item asks for no FORCED-line companion (pkgGRT2 keys on E-COL). The check's reader ends [DR4] at the end of the user text, so fault 3 is lenient for words that stand in text appended after [DR4]. No code decides whether the judge is right to read words as a grant. Not shown by a run.
